data.title: AI Agent
data.tagline: An AI system that can plan steps, use permitted tools, and act on results toward a goal
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish an agent’s model output from tool evidence and define a safe, checkable task for it.
data.description: To fix a page, an agent can read the relevant file, edit it, run a check, and report what passed. It only has the tools, permissions, and context the product gives it.

learning.assumes: You have used a chat assistant or watched one read files and run checks.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish an agent’s model output from tool evidence and define a safe, checkable task for it.

explanation.title: Set a goal and constraints
explanation.text: The product gives the agent a task, protected scope, and the information it needs.

explanation.title: Use permitted tools
explanation.text: The model can request reads, edits, or checks, but the runtime controls what it may do.

explanation.title: Report from evidence
explanation.text: Real tool results, file changes, and tests determine whether the task is actually complete.

explanation.title: AI agent vs chatbot: what is the difference?
explanation.text: A chatbot describes the conversational interface; an AI agent describes a goal-directed workflow that uses results to decide the next step. One product can be both. What it describes: AI Agent — A workflow that takes actions, observes results, and continues toward a goal.; Chatbot — An interface where people and an AI exchange messages.. How work continues: AI Agent — Uses tool output or other observations to choose another action or stop.; Chatbot — Organizes interaction as turns; it may answer directly or provide access to an agent workflow.. Typical workflow: AI Agent — Inspects repository files, edits code, runs tests, and verifies fixes before concluding.; Chatbot — Explains why an error occurred based on text pasted into the chat prompt.. Investigating an application bug: A chatbot can explain an error from the details you provide. An AI agent can take on the goal of fixing it: read files, edit code, run tests, and use the results to decide whether more work is needed. A chat interface may be how you control that agent.

data.boundary: An agent is not automatically authorized or correct. Its permissions, tool results, and verification still determine what it can safely claim.

lessonPractice.title: Which example is best described as an AI agent rather than a single response or a predefined workflow?

options.label: It reads the error and relevant files, then uses test results to decide whether to investigate, edit, or ask for human judgment
options.feedback: Correct. The path is not fixed in advance: the model chooses actions from real observations while tools and stopping conditions still constrain it.

options.label: A model receives one article and returns one summary without external information or follow-up action
options.feedback: That is a single generation, not a loop of actions chosen from environmental feedback.

options.label: Code always runs classify, translate, and send in that order, and the model cannot change the path or choose another tool
options.feedback: That is a predefined workflow: a model participates, but code decides the route in advance.

data.agentPrompt: The cause of this sign-in failure is unclear. Read the error and relevant code first, then choose the checks you need. Run the relevant test after each change. Do not alter unrelated features or read real secrets. Stop when tests pass and show the evidence; ask me before making a product decision.
